items.rationale: The window holds the system prompt, tool definitions, messages and tool results, and the whole of it is sent on each call. Manuals sit outside it until retrieval pulls a chunk in (a, M7), earlier sessions are gone unless notes are loaded (c, M3), and the model never sees the tool's code, which the program runs (d, M4).

A new session starts with an empty window, so information survives only if the program saves it outside the window and loads it back. Trusting the model to remember is M3; a larger window or longer prompt does not carry anything between sessions.

Call 1 input = 1,000 + 100 = 1,100. Call 2 input = 1,100 + 50 + 350 = 1,500. Call 3 input = 1,500 + 200 + 100 = 1,800. Total = 1,100 + 1,500 + 1,800 = 4,400. Answering 1,800 counts only the last call, and forgets the history is resent each time (M9).

Semantic search can miss exact identifiers; keyword matching such as BM25 finds them, and merging the two keeps both strengths. Returning more chunks or pasting every manual adds cost and rot (M7); a prompt instruction cannot change what the search returns (M8).

Clearing removes text from the window for good, so anything that must survive has to be written to notes before it is cleared. A larger window does not help and lets rot grow (M7); unlimited filling ends in overflow; an instruction cannot make a cleared result reappear (M9).
